label: Secrets from the keychain or a mounted file, CI never spends tokens; Docker planned (#94)
decisions: Docker: start with the dev loop, built to grow into production; agent + all 3 apps in Compose, Supabase stays with its CLI (Laurie)
Secrets are delivered as mounted files (<NAME>_FILE, default /run/secrets/<name>), in Docker and production (Laurie)
The most secure order: keychain (local) → mounted file → throwaway local value outside production; never the process environment (Laurie)
The test is 'is it a credential', so URLs carrying a password are secrets and plain URLs are config (mine, approved)
Paid provider keys are refused under CI=true or APP_ENV=ci, a second guard beside the live-test skip (Laurie)
Node reader included in PR 1; SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET moved to the resolver (Laurie)
Unimplemented env settings kept in the examples, marked planned (Laurie)
No ADR until closer to production (Laurie)
Throwaway values allowed in ci as well as local; Node APP_ENV defaults to local; Pexels not refused in CI (mine, flagged in the PR)
Live secret rotation for long-lived clients and pools declined; rotation reaches them at restart (mine, on the #94 thread)

retro.went_well: The design went from an outline to locked decisions in a few short rounds, with each tradeoff put as a question rather than chosen for Laurie. The audit of the .env.example files, done at her request, checked every variable against the code that reads it, and it found a missed secret (SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET) and several stale claims before review did. Every outward write (PR body, three thread replies) was read back exactly.
retro.improve: I repeated the operations example's 'demo refused outside NODE_ENV=test' claim in a summary without checking it, and it was false. Two of Greptile's three findings were things I could have caught myself: the rotation claim ignored the Director client and pools I had read, and the Pexels boundary change let a new exception skip an existing fallback. I also ran cd in Bash twice, against the repo rule.
retro.tooling_suggestion: When changing what a function can raise, grep its callers' except clauses in the same step. Before claiming a behaviour in a summary or a PR body (rotation, a guard), find the code that enforces it, not the doc that describes it.
